question:
In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum, the electric field oscillates with amplitude $48\text{ V m}^{-1}$ and frequency $2.0 \times 10^{10}\text{ Hz}$. Calculate
(i) the wavelength,
(ii) the magnetic field amplitude, and
(iii) show that the average energy density of the electric field is equal to that of the magnetic field.

options.A:
(i) $\lambda=\dfrac{c}{\nu}=\dfrac{3.0\times10^8}{2.0\times10^{10}}=1.5\times10^{-2}\text{ m}$.
(ii) $B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=\dfrac{48}{3.0\times10^8}=1.6\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$.
(iii) $\langle u_E\rangle=\dfrac{1}{4}\varepsilon_0E_0^2\approx5.1\times10^{-9}\text{ J m}^{-3}$ and $\langle u_B\rangle=\dfrac{B_0^2}{4\mu_0}\approx5.1\times10^{-9}\text{ J m}^{-3}$; hence they are equal.
options.B:
(i) $\lambda=1.5\times10^{2}\text{ m}$.
(ii) $B_0=1.6\times10^{-9}\text{ T}$.
(iii) The electric-field energy density is twice the magnetic-field energy density.
options.C:
(i) $\lambda=6.7\times10^{1}\text{ m}$.
(ii) $B_0=1.6\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$.
(iii) $\langle u_E\rangle=5.1\times10^{-9}\text{ J m}^{-3}$ while $\langle u_B\rangle=0$ because magnetic fields carry no energy.
options.D:
(i) $\lambda=1.5\times10^{-2}\text{ m}$.
(ii) $B_0=1.6\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$.
(iii) $\langle u_E\rangle=\dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0E_0^2$ and $\langle u_B\rangle=\dfrac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}$, so the average electric energy density is twice the average magnetic energy density.
